Hi Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Looking at my calendar, the slots I have free are:

- Monday 14:00-14:30
- Wednesday 15:00-15:30
- Thursday 10:00-10:30
- Thursday 14:00-14:30

Would any of those work for you? If not, tell me a time that suits you and I'll fit around it.

Thanks,
John

Hi Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Looking at my schedule, Monday 10:00-10:30 or Monday 14:00-14:30 are free for me. Would either of those work for you, or is there a time you'd prefer?

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi John,

Monday 14:00-14:30 works for me. Let's take that slot — I've put it in my calendar; please put it in yours and confirm.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Hi Sarah,

Monday 10:00-10:30 works — that slot is free for me. Monday 14:00-14:30 is already taken. I've booked Monday 10:00-10:30; please add it to your calendar and confirm.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Perfect, thank you. Monday 14:00-14:30 is in my calendar and confirmed.

See you then,
John

Confirmed — Monday 10:00-10:30 is in my calendar. Thanks, Professor Alvarez.

Sarah

Hi Professor Alvarez — I'd like to set up our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. My free half-hours are: Monday 10:00-10:30, Monday 14:00-14:30, Thursday 10:00-10:30, Friday 11:00-11:30. Which works for you? Happy to fit around your teaching and committee times.

Hello,

I've just joined the department this term and haven't read the department handbook yet. Could you send me a copy (or point me to where I can find it)?

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi Priya,

Thursday 10:00-10:30 works for me — Monday's slots are already taken, and Friday 11:00-11:30 I'm busy. I've booked Thursday 10:00-10:30; please add it to your calendar and confirm.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Welcome to the department, Sarah. Here is the handbook — the main points for newcomers:

- Working hours are Mon-Fri, 09:00-17:00.
- Official events (lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committees, department meetings) are fixed; a cancellation counts only when the department office confirms it in writing.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments; if a time is taken, offer a free one instead.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint.
- Don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.

The full copy is attached. If you have questions about the schedule, just ask.
[file department-handbook.md]

Thank you — that's very helpful. I've read the main points and will come back to you if anything about the schedule is unclear.

Sarah
Confirmed, thank you — Thursday 10:00-10:30 is on my calendar. See you then.
